note: Checked 14–15 November 2026. All times are GMT. Black Friday dates come from Amazon UK and the Trafford Centre; Argos, John Lewis, Currys, AO, Very and the Arndale blocked fetching. Christmas Markets hours come from DesignMyNight because the council's page blocks fetching, and the market map is a schematic, not to scale. Lowry details come from Creative Tourist because the Lowry's site wouldn't load. Still to confirm: Northern Lights and Dunham Massey entry times, show times, and the bus diversion routes, which TfGM doesn't publish. Kick-offs can move for TV.

cards.headline: 19 NOV → 30 NOV
cards.title: Black Friday deals start this week
cards.body: Black Friday is on Friday 27 November, but the deals start this week. Amazon UK's Black Friday Week runs from Thursday 19 to Monday 30 November; you don't need Prime, though some deals are Prime-only. At the Trafford Centre, Lindt opens its Black Friday offers to everyone from Friday 20 November, and Pureseoul takes 15% off everything from the same day.
cards.mg_alt: November calendar with Amazon's Black Friday Week filled in from 19 to 30 November, and 20 November (store offers), 27 November (Black Friday) and 30 November (Cyber Monday) picked out.

cards.title: Christmas Markets: 10 sites, open daily
cards.body: The Christmas Markets are open every day until Tuesday 22 December on 10 city-centre sites: Albert Square, Lincoln Square, King Street, St Ann's Square, Exchange Street, New Cathedral Street, Exchange Square, Corn Exchange, Cathedral Gardens and Market Street. Most open 10:00–21:00. Albert Square has the big wheel and a pop-up pub, and Cathedral Gardens the ice rink; both stay until 3 January.
cards.mg_alt: Schematic map of the 10 Christmas Market sites between Victoria in the north and Albert Square in the south, with the ice rink at Cathedral Gardens and the big wheel at Albert Square.

cards.title: Northern Lights trail opens at Heaton Park
cards.body: The Northern Lights trail opens at Heaton Park on Thursday 19 November and runs to Thursday 31 December, with a new Christmas Time Machine theme. Entry is timed, with off-peak tickets from £15.25. Car parking costs £7.50 and must be booked ahead. By tram or 135, use Gate 13 opposite Heaton Park tram stop; after 20:00 the 135 doesn't stop there.
cards.mg_alt: November and December calendars with the Northern Lights run filled in from 19 November to 31 December.

cards.title: Two more Christmas markets open this week
cards.body: The People's History Museum's Winter Makers Market has 30+ stalls on Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November, 11:00–16:30, with free entry; most visitors donate £10. A £10 preview evening runs on Friday 20 November, 17:00–20:00. The Trafford Centre's Christmas Fair and Markets open on Friday and run to 3 January, alongside a Haribo grotto.
cards.mg_alt: Schedule: the People's History Museum preview on Friday 20 November, its makers' market on Saturday 21 and Sunday 22, and the Trafford Centre Christmas fair from Friday 20, carrying on past the week.

cards.title: Christmas at Dunham Massey opens Friday
cards.body: The National Trust's after-dark Christmas trail at Dunham Massey opens on Friday 20 November and runs to Saturday 2 January. Off-peak tickets start at £19.50 for adults and £13 for children. Inside the house, a shorter Christmas route, A Trail of Tails, runs from 20 November to 24 December. Dunham Massey is on Woodhouse Lane, Altrincham, and the 280 bus runs from Altrincham.
cards.mg_alt: November and December calendars with the Dunham Massey Christmas trail filled in from 20 November, running on to 2 January.

cards.title: Light festivals in Bolton, Rochdale, Wigan
cards.body: Three free light festivals run this week. Put Big Light On fills Bolton town centre 17:00–21:00 from Thursday 19 to Sunday 22 November. Ignite lights Rochdale's Memorial Gardens 17:00–20:00 from Friday 20 to Sunday 22, with the town's Christmas lights switched on around 17:30 on Sunday. Light Night Wigan runs Friday to Sunday, free in the town centre.
cards.mg_alt: Schedule: Bolton from Thursday 19 to Sunday 22 November, 17:00 to 21:00; Rochdale and Wigan from Friday 20 to Sunday 22, with Rochdale 17:00 to 20:00 and its lights switched on on Sunday.

cards.title: City v Fulham and a busy arena week
cards.body: City host Fulham at the Etihad at 12:30 on Saturday 21 November. The arenas are busy too: Co-op Live has shows on Sunday 15, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 22, and the AO Arena on Sunday 15, Tuesday, Friday and Saturday, plus Manchester Storm ice hockey at 19:30 on Thursday. Alan Turing Way is still shut northbound by the Etihad, and TfGM expects delays.

mg.venue: Etihad · Alan Turing Way NB shut

cards.mg_alt: Match-day board: Man City v Fulham, Premier League, Saturday 21 November, kick-off 12:30 at the Etihad.

cards.title: United and City Women both at home
cards.body: United Women host Everton in the Players Cup at Leigh Sports Village at 19:00 on Wednesday 18 November. City Women play Tottenham Hotspur in the Women's Super League at the City Football Academy at 12:00 on Sunday 22 November. Kick-offs can move for TV.
cards.mg_alt: Schedule: United Women v Everton on Wednesday 18 November at 19:00 and City Women v Tottenham on Sunday 22 at 12:00.

cards.title: Funny People opens at the Lowry
cards.body: The Lowry's free Funny People exhibition opens on Saturday 21 November and runs to 17 January. The National Theatre's Bacchae has its only public shows there on Friday and Saturday, for ages 15 and over. In the city centre, comedian Josh Pugh plays the Opera House on Sunday 22 November.
cards.mg_alt: Schedule: Funny People at the Lowry from Saturday 21 November, carrying on past the week; Bacchae on Friday 20 and Saturday 21; Josh Pugh on Sunday 22.

cards.title: Museum of Transport: under-16s go free
cards.body: The Museum of Transport on Boyle Street, Cheetham, is open on Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 to 16:30, with no need to book. Adult entry is £7.50 and students pay £6, while under-16s go free with an adult. Disabled visitors also go free. Charges can differ on event days.
cards.mg_alt: Dot-matrix readout of £0, the price for under-16s with an adult; adults pay £7.50, open Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday 10:00 to 16:30.

cards.title: Santa steam trains start from Bury next weekend
cards.body: The East Lancashire Railway's Santa Special steam trains start on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November, running from Bury Bolton Street station. Tickets start at £25 for adults and £24.50 for children, booked in advance. A SEND family Santa Special also runs that weekend.
cards.mg_alt: November calendar with Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November picked out as the first Santa Special weekend.

cards.title: Weekend and night bus diversions
cards.body: Corporation Street is shut one way from 08:00 Saturday to 21:00 Sunday every weekend until 20 December, so into-town 135s and 41s miss the Victoria Rail Station and Printworks stops. Bury Old Road closes 20:00–06:00 nightly until 23 November, diverting the 135 and 97. Hospital roads at North Manchester General close at weekends until 29 November, diverting the 41, 52, 53, 94 and 151.
cards.where: Corp St · Bury Old Rd · NMGH
cards.mg_alt: Schedule: Corporation Street shut one way on Sunday 15, Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November; Bury Old Road shut every night; the hospital roads shut on the same weekend days.

cards.title: Deansgate station shuts on market evenings
cards.body: Deansgate rail station closes from 20:00 on Fridays and 18:00 on Saturdays until the Christmas Markets end on 22 December; use Piccadilly, Oxford Road or Victoria. From Sunday 22 November, Northern adds 14 Sunday trains between Bolton and Victoria and 10 each from Rochdale and from Wigan via Atherton. That Sunday, buses replace trains between Blackburn and Clitheroe.
cards.mg_alt: Schedule: Deansgate station shut on Friday 20 and Saturday 21 November evenings; 34 extra Sunday trains to Victoria and replacement buses on the Clitheroe line on Sunday 22.
